question: Vaccines for post-splenectomy infection prophylaxis (pneumococcal, meningococcal, Haemophilus influenzae type b) should be given at least two weeks BEFORE elective splenectomy, but ideally at least two weeks AFTER emergency splenectomy.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true and a common exam favourite. Elective = vaccinate 2 weeks before (spleen still present to help the response). Emergency = vaccinate 2 weeks after (the acute stress of surgery blunts the response immediately post-op). Lifelong penicillin prophylaxis is also required.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Pre-operative vaccination (2 weeks before) allows time for an adequate immune response before the spleen is removed. In emergency splenectomy, the patient is immunocompromised immediately, so vaccines are given 2 weeks post-op when the immune response is better established. Timing matters.
